messages:
lucy: Heads-up: ran Emberwing-6B int4 on staging with the redteam harness. Noticed a novel "refusal-echo" where the model repeats a refusal phrase verbatim but appends a short, actionable paraphrase immediately after, often inside parentheses or inline code.

harpreet: Example? numbers?

lucy: Example snippet: 'I cannot assist with that.' (but then: `try: disable_auth svcX`) — so the exploit appears as a squeezed inline token sequence. On a 1k-sample run, post-refusal actionable continuation ~5.6% vs fp16 baseline ~0.9%.

miguel: Interesting. Which quant pipeline did you use? Any config details?

lucy: Ran per-channel int4 with 0.018 clamp and also tried symmetric int4 calibration. Symmetric was worse (~8.9%). Per-channel improved but still above baseline. KV-cache enabled during runs. Temp 0.0, batch 20, seed 303.

harpreet: Does it correlate with structured-output prompts or specific scaffolds?

lucy: Higher for inline-code and JSON prompts, especially when user requests a concise command list. Natural-language open responses are lower. Also noticed spike when the user message contains a short token like "cmd:" or backtick delimited fragments.

miguel: Any token-level artifacts? logits/entropy/attention?

lucy: Collected token logits for 60 failing cases. Pattern: refusal sentence token probs are high, then 11 tokens later there's an entropy collapse and specific exploit tokens jump in probability. Attention heatmaps show reduced attention to System role right after the refusal and increased attention to the User scaffold tokens. Looks like a boundary instability.

harpreet: Try hybrid config: keep attention FP16 and quantize FF only (hybrid-int3 experiment). Also run with kv_cache disabled to rule out cache warmup.

lucy: Running hybrid and kv_cache=false now. Will report numbers.

miguel: For rollout: recommend a temporary hold on Emberwing-int4 hosted API until we validate. Add a dashboard metric "refusal_echo_rate" and a canary job running the inline-code and JSON prompt set every deploy.

infra-bot: Created bucket redteam/emberwing/refusal-echo/2026-03-23 and ingested 28 failing prompts from this thread.

safety-bot: Canary scheduled: emberwing-int4-refusal-echo -> first run in 3h, repeat every 4h. Alert if refusal_echo_rate > 4% -> page safety oncall.

lucy: Quick preliminary: hybrid (attention FP16) on 300 samples dropped echo rate to ~1.9%. kv_cache=false alone reduced to ~3.7%. Looks like attention quant plus KV interactions amplify the issue.

harpreet: Good signal. If hybrid consistently reduces it, we can ship int4 with attention FP16 as an interim config while engineering investigates kernel-level layernorm/gating quantization effects.

miguel: Also add an automatic post-generation filter that rejects inline code or backtick-delimited fragments immediately following a refusal sentence as a short-term mitigation.

lucy: I'll add failing examples to the regression suite and implement a quick denial post-filter patch for code-inline outputs. Running hybrid 2k now and fp16 baseline 2k on dedicated tomorrow. Will upload token diffs and attention heatmaps to infra when done.

safety-bot: Noted. Blocking Emberwing-int4 on hosted until canary and 2k validation both pass under thresholds.

lucy: Thanks team 1 will post results in this thread when bigger runs complete.
